001: Haoran, have you thought about your career plans recently?
Yes, I'm planning to apply for a management position next year.
So have you done anything to prepare for that goal?
I signed up for a leadership training course, hoping to improve myself a bit.
That sounds great. I wish you success in passing the selection.
Thanks. When the time comes, I'll need to ask you for some guidance.
002: Jingyi, what do you think the criteria for promotion are at our company?
Besides performance, I think communication skills and teamwork are also very important.
Then in what areas do I still need to improve?
You could take the initiative to handle more cross-departmental projects.
That makes sense. I always feel like I'm a bit passive.
Be more proactive, and opportunities will naturally increase.
003: Zixuan, do you have any long-term plans for your career development?
I want to go deep into the technical field for a few years first, then move toward management.
So between technology and management, which do you think suits you better?
I prefer technology, but management can bring greater influence.
Combining the two might be the best choice.
Exactly, I'm looking for that balance.
004: Jiaqi, have you attended any professional training recently?
I just finished an advanced course in data analysis.
Do you think this course has been a big help to your work?
It's been a huge help. I'm much more efficient at handling reports now.
Then I should consider learning some new skills too.
Learn more while you're young. It'll definitely come in handy later.
005: Tianyou, do you think changing jobs helps with career development?
It depends. Sometimes changing environments really can bring new opportunities.
But I'm worried that a new company might be unstable, and the risk is too great.
There is some risk, but staying in place is also a risk.
You're right. I need to weigh the pros and cons carefully.
Just make sure you think it through before deciding. Don't be impulsive.
006: Yuxuan, what state do you hope to be in five years from now?
I hope I can become a core member of my department.
Then what abilities do you need to have to reach that goal?
Besides professional skills, leadership and strategic thinking are also crucial.
It seems I need to start consciously developing those.
Starting to plan now is not too late at all.
007: Junjie, do you think the mentorship system helps with our growth?
I think it helps a lot. A mentor's experience can help us avoid detours.
So is there any senior you're thinking of asking to be your mentor?
I plan to ask Manager Wang from the marketing department. He's very experienced.
That's a good idea. I also want to go ask Director Li from R&D.
Listening to advice from seniors is always a good thing.
008: Tingting, are you satisfied with your current salary and benefits?
Fairly satisfied, but I value room for growth more.
So what do you think about our company's development prospects?
The prospects are good. As long as the company does well, there are more opportunities for individuals.
True, the platform matters more than the immediate salary.
Keep your sights set on the long term, and you'll gain more.
009: Haoran, have you considered changing careers recently?
I've thought about it, but I think I should first achieve something in my current field.
Changing careers takes a lot of courage. Are you ready?
Not completely ready yet, so I want to accumulate some experience first.
It's good to be cautious. After all, the cost of changing careers is not low.
Right, I can't be too impulsive. I need to do it in a planned way.
010: Jingyi, do you think further education helps with career development?
It helps, but it also depends on the field of study and actual needs.
I'm considering pursuing a part-time master's degree. Do you think it's worth it?
If it's related to your career goals, then it's worth doing.
My main goal is to improve my theoretical knowledge.
Then go for it. Learning is always beneficial.
